questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It was important for me that there was different classes to choose from, and that there were classes that I had a genuine interest in. It was also important to me that the host university took into account that everyone might not be on the same high level, especially in regards to language skills.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of emails being sent out with the information that you needed, however it also meant that there were a lot of email to go through if you needed to find the right information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I had some help regarding registration for classes.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really difficult to find housing - apparently there is a housing crisis in Scotland, and that wasn't really being told beforehand. We were scammed and was without housing after we arrived in Scotland and was lucky enough we found a quick backup plan.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: That it is really difficult to find housing, and that there might be a lot of fake landlords online trying to take your money.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My process got prolonged because I wasn't aware that you needed to do more than what seemed obvious

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You register on their version of mobility online, and when you've followed all the steps you're classes become visible for you in their system

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I didn't really use a lot of the help offered, but it seemed that help was offered in all aspects; mental health, IT, proof reading of assignments, help for exchange students etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I had applied for an extra class than what I needed to, just to be sure I got what I wanted, and then they wrote back to me and told which classes where at the same time and what they recommended to do and which class to remove, so I ended up with the 3 classes that I wanted from the start.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you are thorough, because you can (apparently) overlook steps, but the people at the university are good to help when needed.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took classes that were for year 3 students, but it was also possible for exchange students to do classes for year 1 and 2, so it was mostly yourself that chose the level of course that you wished for

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
It didn't really. The only similarity was that a professor was teaching the class. 
There wasn't a lot of preparation for class, and it was more voluntary than obligatory to do - you didn't need or weren't expected to buy the books for the classes, and could get them at the library if you wanted to. Even if there was material to be read, the teachers didn't really write out which chapters to read, so I suppose you found a chapter that correlates with the theme of the class

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Housing Law, Sports Law & Law, Film and Popular Culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If possible I would recommend to choose classes that aren't to bound to the country you're in. If there are classes that are more universal, that makes it easier to understand and apply, and to take with you after you go home.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: There wasn't really any

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was less expensive than I expected. Also going out didn't need to be expensive - you could just choose a place that was less expensive, which most of them were

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't take use of them myself but it sounded like there was something for everyone.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a gym on campus plus a lot of other athletic clubs. There were also different scottish events through the semester

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The university has a student union that's really cozy - you can just chill, eat some food, watch sport, play games and it is also possible to get some drinks if you like that.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The highlands and really most of the things Scotland is known for - just search for trips online and there are so many different ones to go on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy since Scotland isn't that different from Denmark when you are not local or moving their permanently.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It seemed like a lot of students were really just doing their own thing, but finding someone to talk to indoor classes might be the easiest way to socialize.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The accents :-)

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That it wasn't the same as Denmark, but still not to far off so that it was all new and scary

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be careful when looking for housing. 
There is another kind of group work going on, but that doesn't have to be a bad thing. 
The exams are hand-written on campus

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The local transportation is way different that in Denmark, and you might need to be patient and open for different kinds of transportation at different times of the day.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Trying to live in another country

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Not losing hope after getting scammed.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
